concerns.text: The Local Non‑Additivity Index (LNAI) is defined as the Pearson correlation between (RF_error − Baseline_error) and the binary presence of a fingerprint bit‑pair (i ∧ j). Because the RF model’s predictions (and thus the residuals) are directly derived from the same fingerprint bits used as predictors, this metric creates a circular validation: it measures how well the model’s own inputs explain its residuals, rather than providing independent evidence of genuine non‑additive chemical interactions. Consequently, the claim that LNAI isolates “interaction zones” where the non‑linear model outperforms the additive baseline is not empirically independent and may overstate the significance of identified bit‑pairs.
